Yes and No.
A lot of typical Chinese fare is still considered fairly cheap by Western standards.
Home style Chinese food “家常菜” (jiachangcai) which is your basic braised meat 红烧肉 (hongshaorou) and tomato egg 番茄炒蛋 (fanqiechaodan) is very delicious and is still pretty cheap overall.
However, even jiachangcai is getting pricey, but that’s just a result of a normal economic progression.
Any 1st tier city in China is going to be several times more expensive than anywhere else in the country.

JiaChangCai in Beijing is going to be at least double the price as it is in Shijiazhuang in nearby Hebei Province.
Hot Pot is another Chinese style food that can get pretty pricey in Beijing unless you’re going with a larger group of people.
A group of 4 at HaidiLao can expect to pay 80 - 120RMB ($12 - $18 USD) per person.
International food has become WAY more popular in recent years and the price that comes with that exotic flare can be pretty steep.
I went to an Indian restaurant recently in Beijing (LOVE Indian food) and racked up a nearly 300 RMB ($46USD) bill by myself.
Don’t get me wrong.
It was delicious, but that’s a good chunk of cash.
There’s also plenty of overpriced Western restaurants with mediocre or plain bad food.
So just go out there and test the waters a little bit.
Not everyone is willing to drop 300RMB on a dope Indian meal once a month, especially if they’re not sure the food is going to be great.

Oh and Nell recommended 糖油饼(sweet fried cake) too!
She said it’s oily, sweet, salty, crunchy… totally a sin.
And… I need to drink something.
Of course 豆浆(soy milk), the best match for a Chinese breakfast.
Oh no… I ate too much… I can’t move.
I don’t think I need lunch.
Bill please.
Now I really need to burn some calories.
It’s weekend.
It’s a good weather.
Best day to explore Beijing.
The Palace Museum!
I long for there.
I search in my Baidu Map App which is an alternative of Google Map here.
It suggests subway.
It costs RMB 5 one way.
The ticket of the Palace Museum is RMB 80 including Treasure Exhibition.
I enjoyed this beautiful palace.
I feel like I took a time machine to this movie ‘The Last Emperor’.
Ohhhh now I’m hungry!
Can’t believe I got hungry again after eating a cow in the morning.
I went to a fast food restaurant.
Nell said typical high-end Chinese restaurants provide meals mostly for groups of people instead of a single person- the amount of one dish is large.
So if I eat alone, a convenient way is to choose fast food such as dumplings and noodles- a proper amount, a reasonable price and a speedy service.
And the best thing is that they taste way better than KFC or Mcdonald’s.
I really ate too much every day since I came to China.
What to do to my increasing meaty belly?
Yes this one!
Mobike- shared bicycles.
It’s really popular lately.
Everybody here wants to try it.
Plus, it’s only RMB 1/hour.
I installed Wechat and Alipay on my phone in advance.
Both provide the E-payment for those shared bicycle systems, internet shopping, and most stores/restaurants.
I found several shared bicycle nearby.
Now I’m cycling to Jingshan Park and Temple of Heaven Park!
I love the spring breeze kissing my face while cycling.
I love to see grandpas and kids neatly playing diabolos in the Temple of Heaven Park.
They invite me to try, calling me ‘Laowai’ with big smiles.
Wow diabolos are difficult, yet so fun.
We laugh a lot.
I start to plan my dinner. (Why food conquers my brain since I came to China?) I long for Beijing Roast Duck.
Its picture is on the cover of my guide book, the No 1.
Beijing Cuisine.
But I know I can hardly eat a whole duck by myself.
Oh I have an idea!
I send a text on Wechat asking my Chinese coworkers if they would like to eat Beijing Roast Duck with me tonight.
Three of them say yes!
The chef slices the duck as fast as a magician.
He does this magic in front of us.
I feel dizzy.
I feel gooooood.
Who said I’m drunk?
Ganbei(Cheers)!
We spent RMB820 on this dinner.
Well, 205/person, in a gorgeous, historical and well-known restaurant, this price is quite reasonable.
After all, I don’t eat Beijing Roast Duck and drink white spirit every day.
Bills please.
Oh My God we are fighting!
My coworkers try all the way to stop me from paying.
They tell me they are locals, ‘the hosts’.
They tell me they will ‘lose face’ if I, as their guest, pay.
Oh that’s crazy!
It’s ME who invited them.
If anything, the ‘host’ should be ME!
Our crazy fight ends up with them promising that they will let me pay next time.
I feel I’m spoiled.
I feel I owe them.
I feel I love owing them now and treating them next time.
I’m so looking forward to next time eating with my dearest Gemenr(bros), toasting, getting dizzy, exchanging silly moments, and feeling connected.
I feel I’m not alone in China.
They call a taxi for me.
We wave ‘huitoujian’ (byebye).
I decide to cut out the ‘car use’ from my Beijing life.
I guess by USD 50, I can hardly live like a king, nor like a ‘foreigner’ who supposes to copy the exact same life style from his/her home country and paste it on Beijing.
And I don’t need nor want to live like that.
I came here to experience a whole different life as a Beijinger.
A not super rich, nor super poor Beijinger.
I saw the news that 2015 average monthly income in Beijing is RMB 7086, which means USD 35 per day. 50 is already above the average.
With 50 dollars, I think I can survive and enjoy a colorful and joyful day.
With the warmth from my Beijng friends, I think I will explore a new me being a Beijinger.
